{{Quote|Calhava bru'chun dralshye'ran!|A Death Watch bomber before leaping to his death|audio=CalhavaBruchunDralshyeran-TMP.flac|<ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref>}}
'''Concordian''' was the common [[Language/Legends|language]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]]<ref name="GttGAR" /> and [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]].<ref name="TMPEG" />

As a dialect of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], the two languages were mutually intelligible, meaning that they were similar enough that an individual speaking one could easily converse with someone speaking the other.<ref name="O66" />

==Overview==
===Known words===
*''gain'' - name<ref name="O66" />
*''neyar'' - my<ref name="O66" />
*''tat'' - brother<ref name="GttGAR" />

===Phrases===
*''Neyar gain Arla Vhett.'' - My name is Arla Fett.<ref name="O66" />
*"Menav nil Menav ni, taan!" - (Untranslated)<ref name="Imperial Commando: 501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Concordian language was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in the [[2004]] novel, ''[[The Cestus Deception]]'', by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Steven Barnes]], where it was referred to as the Mandalorian language by the character [[Sheeka Tull]].<ref name="TCD">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

However, the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic]]'', later [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the language as Concordian.<ref name="GttGAR" /> It is important to note there are multiple origins of "Concordian" now branched under the same name. The Fan created version of which [[Concordian|lines and dialogue]] were used in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]] and the varieties which was used in the novels.

The Concordian name was later applied to the dialect spoken by the residents of Mandalore's moon of Concordia, in the twelfth episode of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]], entitled "[[The Mandalore Plot]]."<ref name="TMPEG" />

At least one Concordian phrase from "The Mandalore Plot"—specifically the line exclaimed by the [[Death Watch bomber/Legends|Death Watch bomber]] before leaping to his [[Death/Legends|death]]—appears to have been drawn from a [[2007]] post on the [http://www.ultimate-empire-at-war.com/forum|Ultimate Empire at War forum] in which a user had compiled a list of [[fanon]] words and translations for the [[Mando'a/Legends|Mandalorian language]].

The aforementioned quote, "Calhava bru'chun dralshye'ran", is translated in the post as "Compassionate [sic] leaders will burn", but although the translation would seem contextually appropriate to the episode's storyline, to date there has been no official confirmation that this is the [[canon]]ically accepted translation.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.ultimate-empire-at-war.com/forum/index.php?topic=912|text=Ultimate Empire at War forum|archivedate=20161124040112}}</ref>
